skill.name: docker-helper
skill.description: Docker Compose generation, Dockerfile optimization, and container troubleshooting guidance.
skill.summary: Generate, review, and troubleshoot Dockerfiles and Docker Compose setups.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, Docker examples, localhost healthchecks, and safe documentation patterns. One high-risk credential example is confirmed because it embeds a literal PostgreSQL password in a Compose connection string. I also found a medium-risk documentation issue where destructive Docker prune commands are shown without safeguards.

remediation.issue: The Compose example includes a literal database password in DATABASE_URL.
remediation.suggestion: Use placeholders such as ${DATABASE_URL} or Docker secrets, and state that sample credentials must be replaced.

remediation.issue: Docker cleanup commands can remove images, build cache, and unused volumes.
remediation.suggestion: Add warnings before docker system prune -a and docker volume prune, or replace them with safer inspection commands.

remediation.issue: Some examples may be copied into production without adaptation.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as templates and require users to review ports, volumes, credentials, and image tags before use.

content.value_statement: Teams often need Dockerfiles and Compose files that match their application structure. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft, review, and troubleshoot container setups.
actual_capabilities: Generate Dockerfile examples for Node.js, Python, and Go applications.
Draft Docker Compose examples for web, API, database, cache, and proxy services.
Recommend multi-stage builds, layer caching, and .dockerignore usage.
Suggest health checks, restart policies, networks, and named volumes.
Provide troubleshooting commands for logs, shell access, service networking, and volume permissions.
Summarize container security practices such as non-root users, pinned tags, and secrets handling.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples; it does not inspect containers by itself.
Generated examples require project-specific review before use.
Sample credentials, ports, and image tags must be replaced for production.
Docker behavior can vary by host operating system and Docker version.

use_cases.title: Containerize a Web Application
use_cases.description: Create a first Dockerfile and Compose file for a service with dependencies.

use_cases.title: Review a Compose Stack
use_cases.description: Check service networking, volumes, health checks, restart policy, and security basics.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Local Containers
use_cases.description: Diagnose startup failures, connection errors, volume permissions, and slow builds.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Dockerfile for this project. Explain the base image, build steps, exposed port, user, and health check.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Compose Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a Docker Compose setup for my web app, API, database, and cache. Include networks, volumes, health checks, and restart policies.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Existing Docker Files
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve build speed and image size.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Dockerfile and Compose file. Suggest changes for multi-stage builds, cache efficiency, image size, permissions, and secrets handling.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Compose Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose why my Compose stack fails to start. Use the logs, service definitions, environment variables, network settings, and volume mappings I provide.

output_examples.input: Create a Dockerfile for a Node.js API.
output: Recommends a multi-stage Node.js build for smaller production images.
Adds a non-root runtime user and a focused health check.
Explains which files should be copied before dependency installation.

output_examples.input: My API cannot connect to Postgres in Docker Compose.
output_examples.output: Explains service-name DNS, shared networks, database readiness, health checks, and connection string review steps.

output_examples.input: Review my Compose file for production readiness.
output: Flags hardcoded credentials and broad host volume mounts.
Suggests pinned image tags, restart policies, and resource limits.
Separates development conveniences from production settings.

best_practices: Replace sample credentials with environment variables, Docker secrets, or a secret manager.
Pin production image versions and rebuild regularly for security updates.
Confirm destructive cleanup commands before running them on shared hosts.
anti_patterns: Copying sample credentials into production Compose files.
Publishing ports or mounting host paths without a security review.
Running Docker cleanup commands on shared hosts without checking impact.

faq.question: Does this skill run Docker commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Commands run only when the active AI tool and user workflow allow execution.

faq.question: Can it create production Docker Compose files?
faq.answer: It can draft production-oriented templates. You must review secrets, ports, volumes, resources, and compliance requirements.

faq.question: Which project types does it cover?
faq.answer: The examples cover Node.js, Python, Go, web services, APIs, databases, caches, and reverse proxies.

faq.question: Can it reduce Docker image size?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests multi-stage builds, smaller base images, cache-friendly layers, and .dockerignore exclusions.

faq.question: Does it handle Docker security?
faq.answer: It gives baseline security guidance, including non-root users, pinned images, vulnerability scanning, and secret handling.

faq.question: What should I check before using generated files?
faq.answer: Review credentials, exposed ports, volume mounts, image versions, resource limits, and environment-specific settings.
